claim_summary: Shearing frames held by a Yorkshire cloth finisher are denounced as machinery that must be destroyed because it displaces skilled croppers.

quote_verbatim: the adoption of certain machinery in the stocking frame, by which one man performed the work of many, and the superfluous labourers were thrown out of employment
claim_summary: Improved stocking frames let one worker do the work of many, throwing the surplus workers out of employment in the Nottinghamshire hosiery trade.

quote_verbatim: the opinion entertained by the labouring class, that the employment of machinery is frequently detrimental to their interests, is not founded on prejudice and error, but is conformable to the correct principles of political economy
claim_summary: The substitution of machinery for labour can reduce the gross produce that funds employment, so displacement of workers is consistent with correct political economy rather than a workers' error.
mechanism_text: conversion of circulating capital, which funds the wage bill, into fixed capital

quote_verbatim: the constant aim and effect of scientific improvement in manufactures are philanthropic, as they tend to relieve the workmen either from niceties of adjustment which exert the eyesight and muscles, or from painful repetition of effort which distort or wear out the frame
quote_locator: The Philosophy of Manufactures, Book I, ch. 1
claim_summary: Mechanical improvement in manufactures relieves workers of arduous tasks rather than displacing them, offering lighter continuous labour at steady wages.
mechanism_text: machinery takes over the physically arduous and precision-demanding elements of the task

quote_verbatim: the introduction of machinery has caused only a temporary displacement of labor, and that in the end more persons are employed than before
quote_locator: First Annual Report of the Commissioner of Labor (1886), section on machinery and labor
claim_summary: The US Commissioner of Labor concludes that machinery displaces labour only temporarily and that employment ultimately rises above its previous level.
mechanism_text: cheapened production expands demand and re-absorbs displaced workers

quote_verbatim: the displacement of labor by machinery has been greater during the last quarter of a century than ever before, and the tendency to over-production may become chronic
quote_locator: Recent Economic Changes, ch. 'Economic Disturbance since 1873'
claim_summary: Machinery is displacing workers faster than they are re-absorbed, and the resulting over-production may become a chronic rather than a cyclical condition.
mechanism_text: productive capacity grows faster than the market can absorb output

quote_verbatim: the introduction of machinery is turning into idleness thousands, faster than new industries are founded, and yet you ask, workingmen to be satisfied
quote_locator: Letter to Judge Peter Grosscup, September 1894
claim_summary: Machinery is idling workers faster than new industries can absorb them, so displacement is outpacing job creation.
mechanism_text: rate of displacement exceeds the rate at which new industries are founded

quote_verbatim: We are being afflicted with a new disease of which some readers may not yet have heard the name, but of which they will hear a great deal in the years to come - namely, technological unemployment. But this is only a temporary phase of maladjustment.
quote_locator: Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren, section II
claim_summary: Labour-saving discovery is outrunning the discovery of new uses for labour, producing technological unemployment, which Keynes expects to be a temporary phase of maladjustment rather than a permanent condition.
horizon_stated_text: in the years to come; a temporary phase of maladjustment
mechanism_text: means of economising the use of labour outrunning the pace at which we can find new uses for labour

quote_verbatim: technological unemployment is a bogey; in the long run technological progress creates more jobs than it destroys
quote_locator: Technology Review, December 1938 (as quoted in MIT Technology Review, 27 January 2024)
claim_summary: Technological progress creates more employment than it destroys over the long run, so technological unemployment is a false alarm.
mechanism_text: new industries founded on new technologies absorb more workers than the displaced trades shed

quote_verbatim: This apparatus is extremely flexible, and susceptible to mass production, and will undoubtedly lead to the factory without employees; as for example, the automatic automobile assembly line. claim_summary: Programmable automatic machinery will produce factories without employees, and under existing industrial arrangements the resulting unemployment would be disastrous.
mechanism_text: flexible, mass-producible automatic control apparatus replaces the human operator on the assembly line

quote_verbatim: Automation is a new and more advanced stage of technological progress, and unless we manage it wisely it can bring mass unemployment and economic chaos rather than the abundance it makes possible
quote_locator: Testimony, Automation and Technological Change hearings, October 1955
claim_summary: Automation can deliver either abundance or mass unemployment depending on whether its introduction is deliberately managed; unmanaged, it threatens large-scale displacement.
mechanism_text: the pace of automation outruns the economy's capacity to create replacement employment

quote_verbatim: Technologically, as I have argued earlier, machines will be capable, within twenty years, of doing any work that a man can do.
quote_locator: The New Science of Management Decision (1960), p. 38
claim_summary: Within twenty years machines will be capable of performing any work a human can perform.

quote_verbatim: the role of humans as the most important factor of production is bound to diminish in the same way that the role of horses in agricultural production was first diminished and then eliminated by the introduction of tractors
claim_summary: Humans' role as the most important factor of production will diminish as computers and automation spread, on the pattern by which tractors first reduced and then eliminated the horse.
mechanism_text: successive waves of more capable machines substitute for human labour as they once substituted for animal power

quote_verbatim: We are entering a new phase in world history - one in which fewer and fewer workers will be needed to produce the goods and services for the global population
claim_summary: Ever fewer workers will be required to produce the world's goods and services, moving the global economy toward a near-workerless condition.
horizon_stated_text: in the years ahead; the early decades of the twenty-first century
mechanism_text: information technology and automation raise output per worker faster than demand for labour grows

quote_verbatim: According to our estimate, 47 percent of total US employment is in the high risk category, meaning that associated occupations are potentially automatable over some unspecified number of years, perhaps a decade or two.
claim_summary: 47 percent of total US employment falls in a high-risk category of occupations that are potentially automatable over perhaps a decade or two.
horizon_stated_text: over some unspecified number of years, perhaps a decade or two
mechanism_text: occupations whose tasks face no near-term engineering bottleneck in perception and manipulation, creative intelligence, or social intelligence become automatable

horizon_stated_text: over the next ten to twenty years
mechanism_text: applies the Frey-Osborne occupational computerisation probabilities to UK occupational employment

quote_verbatim: journalists and even expert commentators tend to overstate the extent of machine substitution for human labor and ignore the strong complementarities between automation and labor that increase productivity, raise earnings, and augment demand for labor
claim_summary: Commentary overstates machine substitution for labour and ignores complementarities that raise productivity and increase labour demand.
mechanism_text: automation complements the tasks it does not replace, raising productivity and the demand for labour in those tasks

quote_locator: OECD Social, Employment and Migration Working Paper No. 189, p. 4

mechanism_text: automatability assessed on the task composition of individual jobs rather than on occupational averages

quote_verbatim: It's just completely obvious that within five years deep learning is going to do better than radiologists. It might be 10 years, but we've got plenty of radiologists already.

claim_summary: Deep learning will outperform radiologists within five years, so training of new radiologists should stop now.
mechanism_text: deep learning surpasses human performance on the image-interpretation task that defines the occupation

magnitude_unit: percent of jobs at high risk

mechanism_text: measured occupational churn rates have fallen rather than risen over the period of the automation forecasts

mechanism_text: generative AI substitutes for a share of the task content of exposed occupations
